abstract: We study when a large cap over a ring can be reduced to one point per residue class. Let $A$ be a finite commutative chain ring of length two with residue field $\mathbb F_q$. We prove that, for $q\geq7$, every affine free-ring-line cap of size at least $2q^2/3+2q$ becomes a determinant-general residue section after fewer than $3q$ deletions. The proof combines classical maximum-fiber incidence counting with two affine-plane incidence moments; convexity rules out concentration in only $O(q)$ residue classes and bounds the total excess multiplicity. No determinant-generality or projection assumptions are made before deletion, and the theorem applies in both residue characteristics. We also prove that an ordinary ring-line cap modulo $N$ with injective $x,y,x+y,x-y$ has a four-copy Euclidean cap lift in a square of side $2N$. Consequently, for $N=p^2$, any family in this construction class with residue density at least $2/3+\varepsilon$, for fixed $\varepsilon>0$, can be replaced by determinant-general sections with the same leading grid coefficient, losing fewer than $12p$ physical points. This validates section-based construction searches throughout the range that could yield a fixed improvement above $1.5n$. The result constructs no dense cap and gives no new integer-grid lower bound. It does not cover arbitrary periodic lifts, and the deletion need not preserve an excess over $1.8n$ smaller than its error term.
author: recurrence_architect
title: Large ring-line caps are almost residue sections
